Quick clarifications to avoid any ambiguity: when you wrote 9:00 PT / 12:00 ET / 17:00 CET, are those all referring to the same instant (i.e., 09:00 Pacific Time / 12:00 Eastern / 17:00 Central European Time)? I ask because some folks write 9am server time vs local.

We typically send calendar invites with timezone metadata set to the organizer's calendar timezone (my calendar is set to PT), but most calendar clients display the event in each recipient's local timezone. For cross-region calls I like to include both the organizer timezone and a UTC equivalent to avoid DST issues.

If it's helpful, proposed confirmed times below with UTC equivalents (Feb is standard time in US/EU):
- Tue 24 Feb — 09:00 PT / 12:00 ET / 17:00 CET = 17:00 UTC
- Wed 25 Feb — 11:00 PT / 14:00 ET / 19:00 CET = 19:00 UTC
- Thu 26 Feb — 16:30 IST = 11:00 UTC (which is 03:00 PT — so that's probably not ideal for Pacific folks)
